slides.title: Let's Measure
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 2 English, Unit 5: Let's Measure. In this unit you learn to count in tens all the way to one hundred. You name the shapes circle, square, triangle, rectangle and heart, and you spot patterns that repeat. Best of all, you learn to measure and compare: which is bigger, which is longer, which is taller and which is heavier. You measure with a ruler in centimetres and metres, ask “How many…?” and answer with There is or There are, and you sort out the number words that sound like other words. Measuring carefully helps us understand the world and be fair to everyone, just like Amal and her friends in this unit's story, “A Fair Way to Measure”. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Count in tens from ten to one hundred, and choose the right number word when two words sound the same.
Name and describe the shapes circle, square, triangle, rectangle and heart.
Notice, continue and describe a pattern that repeats.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to count in tens from ten to one hundred, and choose the right number word when two words sound the same. You will also name and describe the shapes circle, square, triangle, rectangle and heart. You will also notice, continue and describe a pattern that repeats. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Words to learn
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: park, dark, card, start, number, add. Listen to each word, look at what it means, and try to use it when you talk and write.

slides.title: Read and think
bullets: Point to the words that show it
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes Shapes All Around Us and A Counting Song. Read slowly, look at the pictures, and find the big idea in each text. When you answer a question, point to the words that show it.

slides.title: Comparing Two Things (-er than)
bullets: When we measure, we usually want to say which of two things is bigger, longer, taller or heavier. To compare two things we add -er to the describing word,...
Try it in your own sentences
slides.narration: The first language focus is Comparing Two Things (-er than). When we measure, we usually want to say which of two things is bigger, longer, taller or heavier. To compare two things we add -er to the describing word, and then we use the word than. Look at the examples, then try the pattern in your own sentences.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Say it, write it, make it better
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1 — Count in Tens. Say your ideas clearly and listen to your partner. In writing, you will draw, trace, copy or write, then check your work with a grown-up or the AI tutor.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the words, then the reading and the questions, then the grammar, speaking and writing. Ask the AI tutor for help any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
